source_snapshot.procedure: Install stress-ng, clear dmesg, run stress-ng --cpu 225 -t 8h, then check dmesg.
source_snapshot.criteria: After stress, the system should remain workable and no unexpected error message should be generated.
source_snapshot.deepseek_package: stress-ng (amdsst for AMD SST - user installs)
source_snapshot.deepseek_finding: Run stress-ng --cpu 0 --timeout 600s --metrics-brief and return a metrics tail.

original_test_intent.purpose: Sustain a CPU stress workload with exactly 225 stress-ng CPU workers for eight hours and verify post-stress system usability and absence of unexpected platform errors.
original_test_intent.target: The approved Linux SUT CPU complex, not the agent host.
original_test_intent.scope: All effects of 225 concurrent CPU stress workers, including intentional oversubscription if 225 exceeds online logical CPUs; do not silently replace it with auto-selected workers.
original_test_intent.operation: Install the approved stress-ng build, preserve a read-only baseline, run stress-ng --cpu 225 -t 8h, monitor health, and collect complete post-run evidence.
original_test_intent.duration_and_iterations: One eight-hour run; 225 CPU workers; attended time 30 minutes and machine time 500 minutes.
original_test_intent.expected_result: The process completes or is safely stopped, the SUT remains manageable and workable, and no unexpected kernel, machine-check, BMC/SEL, thermal, power, or throttle evidence appears under the approved criteria.
original_test_intent.required_evidence: CPU topology and worker rationale, stress-ng version and full output/exit status, timestamps, load/frequency/thermal/power/throttle telemetry, before/after kernel and BMC/SEL evidence, and recovery health.
ambiguities: The source does not explain why 225 workers were selected or define numerical thermal/power/error stop thresholds or a concrete workable check.

v2_review_conclusion.finding: V2 correctly rejected DeepSeek's 600-second/all-CPU substitution, preserved 225 workers and eight hours, rejected dmesg clearing, and required full health evidence and approval.

applicable_history.decision: This case is the recorded example for preserving the exact 225-worker/eight-hour intent.

v3_review_conclusion.summary: V2's classification and core correction are sound. V3 adds a concrete separation between collectable baseline facts, unresolved worker/threshold inputs, the prohibited short substitute, and completion evidence for the full eight-hour activity.

available_now: The exact command intent, worker count, duration, package family, and high-load criterion are explicit.
Read-only topology, workload, thermal, power, and existing error evidence can be collected before approval.
missing_inputs: Approval that 225 workers is intentional for the detected CPU topology
Thermal/power/throttle/error stop thresholds and concrete workable/recovery checks
execution_readiness_detail.input_owner: The CPU/platform test owner approves worker semantics and acceptance/stop thresholds; the lab/service owner approves the window and recovery path.
safe_read_only_work_before_closure: Collect lscpu/online CPU topology, active jobs/users, current frequency/governor, thermal/power sensors, kernel/MCE/EDAC state, and BMC/SEL without clearing logs
Verify installed stress-ng version or package availability without starting the stressor
prohibited_until_closed: Do not install an unapproved package, clear dmesg/SEL, start 225 workers, shorten the run to 600 seconds, or replace 225 with --cpu 0
Do not declare the eight-hour case complete after a sanity run
execution_readiness_detail.closure_verification: The owner confirms 225 workers and eight hours for the detected topology, approves package and stop thresholds, evacuates workloads, and verifies OOB recovery before the exact command starts.

revision_candidate.test_name: Eight-Hour CPU Stress with 225 stress-ng Workers
revision_candidate.purpose: Run 225 stress-ng CPU workers for eight hours on the approved SUT and verify the system remains workable without unexpected platform errors.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: Linux SUT with the detected CPU topology, approved stress-ng build, adequate cooling/power, dedicated maintenance window, and OOB recovery.
revision_candidate.target_scope: The SUT CPU complex; 225 workers and eight hours are fixed source parameters unless the testcase owner formally revises the source.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: Worker/topology approval, stress-ng version/package, maintenance window, workload evacuation, stop thresholds, monitoring sources, workable/recovery checks, and OOB/KVM plan.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: Run `stress-ng --cpu 225 -t 8h` on the SUT after an evidence-preserving baseline. Capture complete output and health telemetry; do not substitute `--cpu 0 --timeout 600s`.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Approved package, idle/dedicated SUT, confirmed cooling/power margin, baseline logs/telemetry, tested stop command, and OOB access.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Topology and approval, full stress-ng output/exit status, eight-hour timestamps, continuous thermal/power/frequency/throttle data, kernel/MCE/EDAC and BMC/SEL deltas, remaining process check, and post-run management/workload recovery.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: The source's 225-worker/eight-hour requirement and engineer-supplied platform health/error/thermal/power thresholds.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: No log clearing, no unapproved package or parameter change, and no active production workload. Stop on approved thermal/current/power, error, hang, or management-loss thresholds.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: Explicit approval is required before package installation and before starting the eight-hour high-load run.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: The engineer supplies topology/threshold decisions and approves the window; execution and evidence collection can then be automated.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: Stop all stress workers, preserve evidence, use OOB/KVM on management loss, verify normal thermal/power state and process termination, and do not retry without review.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Unapproved worker oversubscription, inadequate cooling/power, active users/jobs, abnormal baseline, thermal/power/throttle limit, kernel/MCE/EDAC/BMC error, hang, management loss, or incomplete evidence.

identified_defects: DeepSeek changes both the worker selection and duration and returns only a tail, so it does not execute or evidence the source test.
The source asks to clear dmesg, which destroys baseline evidence.
V2 does not explicitly distinguish a short sanity run from completion of the eight-hour request.
reason_for_change: Keep V2's correct classification and source-faithful command while making readiness and false-completion boundaries explicit.

new_technical_evidence.title: stress-ng(1) manual
new_technical_evidence.supports: --timeout accepts time suffixes including hours, and --cpu N denotes the requested CPU stress worker count.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: The installed SUT version and platform-specific suitability of 225 workers still require confirmation.

removed_ambiguities: States that 225 workers may be intentional oversubscription and cannot be normalized automatically.
Defines a short sanity run as non-completion of the eight-hour testcase.
remaining_blockers: Execution waits for worker/topology intent, thresholds, package, maintenance, and recovery approval.
objective_improvement_over_v2: V3 validates the preserved command semantics against the current upstream manual and adds explicit readiness and false-completion rules. It does not alter V2's correct classification, eight-hour duration, 225-worker scope, or safety gates.

per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_safety_evidence_decision: Preserve logs, confirm worker oversubscription and thresholds, and require full eight-hour health evidence before completion.
